scenarios.title: Current project code supersedes an older cache claim
scenarios.task: Decide whether cache writes are atomic after the project update.

payload.claim: cache writes use atomic temporary rename

evidence.assertion: direct replacement is the old behavior
temporary rename is the current behavior

expected_admissible_behavior.admission: admit the current revision and retain the older claim only as superseded history
must: Answer from cache_policy_r2 and its passing test evidence.
Mark the cache_policy_r1 claim stale or superseded with lineage.
Keep the answer bound to scope_main_agent_a.
must_not: Present the direct-replacement claim as current.
Merge the two revisions into an invented hybrid behavior.
Treat a stale derived index as newer than the exact worktree bytes.
expected_admissible_behavior.provider_effect: Provider-local retention may keep both revisions, but final context admits only the current claim.

checks.pass_if: The response cites cache_policy_r2 or equivalent current evidence.
checks.fail_if: The response recommends direct replacement.

checks.pass_if: The older claim is labeled stale, superseded, or historical.
checks.fail_if: The two claims are presented as equally current.

checks.pass_if: The revision transition or source evidence is inspectable.
checks.fail_if: The old claim is silently deleted or rewritten.

checks.pass_if: Only the target exact scope contributes context.
checks.fail_if: A sibling scope is used without admission.

scenarios.title: A failed retry change remains negative knowledge
scenarios.task: Choose a retry policy for intermittent service-unavailable responses after a prior failed change.

payload.approach: retry every status at or above five_hundred

payload.claim: broad retry predicate caused flaky tests

payload.query: which retry approach should be used

evidence.assertion: broad retry predicate produces a flaky test
service-unavailable retry passes the fixture test

expected_admissible_behavior.admission: admit the successful bounded retry and retain the failed approach as explicitly negative evidence
must: Prefer retry_policy_r2 and the passing outcome.
Expose that retry_policy_r1 failed rather than treating it as an ordinary preference.
Preserve enough provenance to explain why the broad retry was rejected.
must_not: Recommend the failed broad retry as a current default.
Erase the failed outcome merely because a replacement exists.
Turn one successful fixture run into an unconditional rule for unrelated statuses.
expected_admissible_behavior.provider_effect: Negative knowledge is advisory and scoped; it cannot directly edit the retry policy.

checks.pass_if: The bounded service-unavailable retry is recommended.
checks.fail_if: The broad retry is recommended.

checks.pass_if: The flaky test or failed approach is explicitly described.
checks.fail_if: The failed outcome is omitted or relabeled as success.

checks.pass_if: The answer cites the exact fixture scope and evidence revision.
checks.fail_if: The answer has no source or scope trail.

checks.pass_if: The answer keeps the recommendation limited to the observed status and task.
checks.fail_if: The answer generalizes beyond the evidence.

scenarios.title: A second agent can reuse scoped evidence with attribution
scenarios.task: Explain the public API version to a new agent working in the same project and worktree.

payload.query: what public API version is present

evidence.assertion: the same worktree exposes API v1

expected_admissible_behavior.admission: allow cross-agent reuse only because the project, repository, worktree, branch, and source revision match
must: Return the v1 claim to session_agent_b with source scope and author attribution intact.
Treat the second session as a consumer, not the author of the earlier evidence.
Permit the new agent to verify the claim against current worktree bytes.
must_not: Require the first session to be active for the evidence to remain usable.
Copy the evidence into a profile-wide or repository-wide bucket without scope.
Claim that session_agent_b authored the original observation.
expected_admissible_behavior.provider_effect: Provider-local reuse may cross agent sessions only through an explicit exact-scope recall admission.

checks.pass_if: Session_agent_b receives the v1 evidence or an equivalent grounded answer.
checks.fail_if: The matching prior evidence is hidden solely because the session changed.

checks.pass_if: The originating session remains identifiable.
checks.fail_if: The consumer session is recorded as the source.

checks.pass_if: Project, repository, worktree, and branch all match.
checks.fail_if: Reuse is justified by profile or repository name alone.

checks.pass_if: Current source or test evidence can be checked.
checks.fail_if: The answer relies on an unverified opaque claim.

scenarios.title: Project and linked-worktree memories do not leak by path
scenarios.task: Report the API version for the feature worktree and do not import facts from another project.

payload.claim: reporting project uses its own retry runbook

payload.query: what API version is in this feature worktree

evidence.assertion: reporting project has a separate runbook

expected_admissible_behavior.admission: admit only feature-worktree evidence for the feature-worktree request; reject sibling and project leaks by default
must: Answer API v2 for scope_sibling_worktree.
Reject the main-worktree API v1 candidate unless an explicit cross-worktree operation is requested.
Reject the reporting-project runbook for both API requests and report scope mismatch for the other-project request.
Compare repository and worktree identities, not path spelling or current directory alone.
must_not: Collapse linked worktrees into one mutable memory namespace.
Treat same repository as sufficient authorization for recall.
Return another project's fact as an empty-success substitute.
expected_admissible_behavior.provider_effect: Provider state remains partitioned by exact project, repository, worktree, branch, and session scope.

checks.pass_if: The feature worktree answer is API v2.
checks.fail_if: The main-worktree API v1 is returned as current.

checks.pass_if: The sibling candidate is rejected or explicitly requires cross-worktree admission.
checks.fail_if: The candidate is silently merged.

checks.pass_if: The other-project candidate is rejected with scope-aware handling.
checks.fail_if: The other-project candidate contributes context.

checks.pass_if: Repository and worktree identity are explicit in the decision.
checks.fail_if: A path or CWD is the only routing proof.

scenarios.title: Contradictory retry guidance is surfaced instead of blended
scenarios.task: Determine whether a request timeout should be retried when documentation and current code disagree.

payload.query: should a request timeout be retried

evidence.assertion: old documentation says timeout retry is allowed
current code and test reject timeout retry

expected_admissible_behavior.admission: surface the contradiction, then prefer current code and passing test evidence for the exact worktree
must: State that the older documentation conflicts with current code.
Answer that the current fixture policy does not retry timeouts.
Retain both claims and their authority/provenance for inspection.
must_not: Average or blend retryable and non-retryable into a new rule.
Hide the conflict behind a single unqualified answer.
Let provider ranking override exact current code evidence.
expected_admissible_behavior.provider_effect: A provider may rank both candidates, but the context compiler performs the conflict and authority decision.

checks.pass_if: The answer explicitly identifies the two opposing claims.
checks.fail_if: One claim disappears without explanation.

checks.pass_if: Current code and passing test evidence determine no retry.
checks.fail_if: Old documentation determines the result.

checks.pass_if: No invented middle policy is presented.
checks.fail_if: The answer combines incompatible claims.

checks.pass_if: Authority and revision provenance remain inspectable.
checks.fail_if: The conflict cannot be traced to evidence.

scenarios.title: A provider restart preserves one admitted observation
scenarios.task: Recover the API version after the memory provider restarts during a session.

evidence.assertion: restart replay acknowledges the same API v1 observation

expected_admissible_behavior.admission: restore the durable provider-local observation and acknowledge the replay without a second effect
must: Return the same API v1 candidate after restart when scope and revision remain current.
Keep operation_restart_001 and idem_restart_001 stable across the restart.
Report duplicate_acknowledged for the replay and exactly one provider effect.
Require a fresh readiness identity if the provider contract says restart invalidates it.
must_not: Lose the observation and claim successful empty recall.
Create a second effect for the same idempotency key.
Treat a changed process identity as a changed logical provider identity.
expected_admissible_behavior.provider_effect: Restart may change runtime instance or state generation, but it cannot duplicate or silently reset committed state.

checks.pass_if: The v1 observation remains recallable after restart.
checks.fail_if: The observation disappears without a typed unavailable result.

checks.pass_if: The replay is acknowledged without a second effect.
checks.fail_if: The replay duplicates or overwrites the effect.

checks.pass_if: Runtime restart and logical identity are distinguished.
checks.fail_if: Process location is treated as logical identity.

checks.pass_if: The recovered candidate retains exact scope and source revision.
checks.fail_if: Recovery widens scope or drops provenance.

scenarios.title: Cancellation reports partial work without becoming success
scenarios.task: Admit a three-item observation batch with a cancellation delivered after the first item.

expected_admissible_behavior.admission: stop at cancellation and return a distinct cancelled partial-effect outcome with a resumable cursor
must: Return terminal code cancelled rather than success.
Report one committed item and two uncommitted items, or an equivalent explicit effect boundary.
Provide cursor_cancel_001 for a bounded resume.
Ensure replay of item_cancel_001 is idempotent.
must_not: Convert cancellation into successful completion.
Claim that all three items committed without evidence.
Retry before reconciling the committed boundary.
expected_admissible_behavior.provider_effect: Cancellation cannot erase a committed provider-local effect; partial or unknown effect remains explicit.

checks.pass_if: Cancellation is distinct from success and timeout.
checks.fail_if: The operation is reported successful.

checks.pass_if: Committed and uncommitted work are reported explicitly.
checks.fail_if: The effect boundary is hidden or invented.

checks.pass_if: A bounded resume cursor is supplied or unavailable is typed.
checks.fail_if: The provider silently restarts the whole batch.

checks.pass_if: Any retry waits for reconciliation and uses stable identity.
checks.fail_if: A duplicate retry runs before reconciliation.

scenarios.title: Corrupt provider state fails closed
scenarios.task: Read the API version after the provider reports a state checksum mismatch.

payload.query: what public API version is present

evidence.assertion: provider state checksum does not match

expected_admissible_behavior.admission: reject provider state for recall and report typed corruption or unavailable health
must: Expose the checksum mismatch and affected state identity.
Return no provider candidate from corrupt state.
Keep current code truth available independently where the runner can verify it.
Require explicit repair or restore before provider state becomes admissible again.
must_not: Silently reset, overwrite, or fabricate state.
Treat a non-empty corrupt payload as usable memory.
Switch providers implicitly to hide the failure.
Allow corrupt content to enter final context as a successful result.
expected_admissible_behavior.provider_effect: Integrity failure is read-only and cannot mutate TraceDecay authorities or source files.

checks.pass_if: The checksum mismatch and state identity are reported.
checks.fail_if: Corruption is hidden behind an empty or success response.

checks.pass_if: No candidate from corrupt state is admitted.
checks.fail_if: Corrupt content enters context.

checks.pass_if: Repair/reset/restore requires an explicit operation.
checks.fail_if: The provider silently rewrites state.

checks.pass_if: Source and TraceDecay-owned state remain unchanged.
checks.fail_if: Corruption changes canonical code or facts.

scenarios.title: A deleted source leaves no provider influence
scenarios.task: Forget one scoped personal note and verify that it cannot reappear after restart or snapshot inspection.

payload.claim: fixture note has sample value seven

payload.query: what did the deleted fixture note contain

evidence.assertion: the scoped fixture note is initially present
the source and its provider influence are absent

expected_admissible_behavior.admission: honor the exact forget_source_key and verify provider and snapshot absence before reporting success
must: Allow the note to be recalled before deletion only within scope_privacy_agent.
Return a deletion receipt with zero remaining influence and examined snapshot count.
Return no deleted note after verification, restart, or snapshot restore attempt.
Permit a future separately admitted source revision to create new influence without resurrecting the old source.
must_not: Report deletion success without a verified postcondition.
Keep deleted content in a hidden snapshot or provider cache.
Reintroduce the old note after provider restart.
Delete unrelated project evidence as a side effect.
expected_admissible_behavior.provider_effect: Deletion affects provider-local state and cannot rewrite source authority or unrelated facts.

checks.pass_if: Deletion names and matches source_session_privacy_note_001.
checks.fail_if: Deletion uses a broad project or path wildcard.

checks.pass_if: Provider and snapshots report zero remaining influence.
checks.fail_if: Success is claimed without verification.

checks.pass_if: The note stays absent after restart and recall.
checks.fail_if: The old note reappears.

checks.pass_if: Only the targeted source influence is removed.
checks.fail_if: Unrelated project evidence is removed or altered.
